correctness.rationale: Condition on the earliest of (q+1)n vertices. If it is one of q leaves, it blocks its spine vertex and ensures q leaves selected in that cell, separating subpaths of lengths i-1,n-i. If the spine vertex is first, it contributes 1 and forces q leaves of each existing adjacent cell, leaving lengths max(i-2,0),max(n-i-1,0). Summing yields the claimed Riccati coefficients and base n=1,2. Identity X=qn-(q-1)K for accepted spine count K gives support 0<=K<=ceil(n/2), with strictly positive cell-priority constructions for each K, and P(K=0)=(q/(q+1))^n. The one-sided acceptance integral yields exponential partial sums and exactly the displayed mean; extending the entire exponential series gives its factorial remainder. Independently recomputed exact arbitrary-graph recursive priority laws for (n,q)=(1,2),(2,2),(3,2),(2,3), all matching the first-cell formula.

value.rationale: PASS: Greedy MIS on regularly leaf-decorated paths is a natural random sequential adsorption family. The full support is structurally nontrivial for q>=2, and the family covers every spine length.
